answer: A farm that wants 274 keys as a result pays 274 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the ripple seed, the terrace timing is verifiable from the karst record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 102 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
